title: Log analyzer
intro: You are reading a web server's request log. Each line has six space-separated fields: an ISO timestamp, a user id, an HTTP method, a path, the latency in milliseconds and the status code. Use only the standard library. Each level extends the previous one.
rules: A line is valid only if it has exactly six fields, the timestamp parses with `datetime.fromisoformat`, and the latency and status are whole numbers. Skip every other line without raising an error.
Keep the input order unless a level says otherwise.

levels.title: Parse request log lines
levels.prompt: Write `parse_log(lines)` that returns a list of dicts with the keys `time` (the original string), `user`, `method`, `path`, `ms` (int) and `status` (int), one per valid line, in input order. Invalid lines are skipped.
edgeCases: "abc" as a latency makes the line invalid
A line with five or seven fields is invalid

levels.title: Requests and average latency per endpoint
levels.prompt: Write `endpoint_stats(records)` that returns a dict keyed by path, in alphabetical order of the path. Each value is a dict with `requests` (how many), `avg_ms` (the average latency rounded to 1 decimal) and `errors` (how many responses had a status of 500 or more).
edgeCases: A 404 is not counted as an error

levels.title: Sessionize users with a 30-minute gap
levels.prompt: Write `sessionize(records, gap_minutes=30)` that groups each user's requests into sessions. A new session starts when the time since the user's previous request is MORE than `gap_minutes` minutes (exactly 30 minutes still continues the session). Return a dict keyed by user (alphabetical) whose value is a list of sessions in time order; a session is a dict with `start` and `end` (the first and last timestamp strings) and `requests` (how many). Sort each user's requests by time first.
levels.signature: def sessionize(records: list[dict], gap_minutes: int = 30) -> dict[str, list[dict]]
edgeCases: A user with one request has one session with start == end
A gap of exactly 30:00 stays in the same session
